_note: The `files` error catalog — every code the module can settle with, its `recoverable` verdict, and the capabilities each platform genuinely lacks (parity/F03-files.md §3c, §5). Two things drift silently when they are not pinned: a code that means `retry is worth offering` on one renderer and `give up` on another, and a platform quietly no-opping a capability it cannot perform. `recoverable` is the contract a surface branches on, so it lives in the shared core (FILE_ERROR_RECOVERABLE) and all three runners assert their table against this file. `unsupportedByPlatform` is the typed-absence roster (durability P4): the named capability resolves `unsupported_platform` with a real message on that platform — never a fake success, never a silent no-op. An empty list means the platform performs every capability.

not_found._note: The path names nothing. Terminal: retrying the same read finds the same nothing.

permission_denied._note: The OS refused, or the root is read-only (`bundle:`). Terminal from the module's side — a permission a user can grant is asked for by the module that owns it, not retried blindly here.

no_space._note: The free-space PRE-CHECK failed before a large write, not an exception caught after a partial one. Recoverable: the user can free space and retry, and the destination is untouched.

is_directory._note: A file operation was aimed at a directory. Terminal: the caller asked the wrong question.

not_directory._note: A directory operation was aimed at a file, or a parent segment is a file. Terminal.

exists._note: The destination already exists and `overwrite` was not set. Recoverable: the same call with `overwrite: true` succeeds, which is exactly the retry a surface offers.

hash_mismatch._note: A verified download landed with the wrong sha256. The partial is removed; a retry is worth offering because the usual cause is a truncated or middlebox-rewritten body.

network_failed._note: The transfer could not complete. The destination is left with NO partial file; `resume: true` picks up from the persisted resume data on the next attempt.

http_error._note: The request reached the server and the server refused it — any status outside 2xx. Distinct from network_failed on purpose: the transport worked, so `resume` is meaningless and the remedy is the STATUS, which rides on `data` as { status, headers, body? } (the body is the server's own explanation, truncated). Recoverable because a 401/429/503 is routinely fixed by refreshing a token or waiting; a caller that wants to give up on a 404 branches on `data.status`, which is exactly why the status is carried rather than folded away. The destination is untouched: the refused body is discarded, never moved into place.

unsupported_root._note: The path is not addressable: an unknown root token, a malformed path, or an attempt to escape the root. Terminal, and deliberately ONE code for every shape of that attempt — a probing caller learns nothing from the distinction.

unsupported_platform._note: The reserved kernel code for a capability this platform genuinely lacks. Terminal, and honest: the caller branches on the code rather than string-matching a message.

capabilities.shared: The `shared:` root — an App Group container on iOS, the app's own external files directory on Android. The web has no second sandbox to share into.
capabilities.exclude: Marking a path as excluded from device backup. iOS has `isExcludedFromBackupKey`; Android backup is declared per-app in the manifest, not per-file, and the web has no backup plane at all.
capabilities.background: A transfer that survives the app being suspended. iOS uses a background `URLSession`, Android a WorkManager foreground worker; a browser tab that is closed takes its fetch with it, so `download`/`upload` still run on the web but the `background: true` guarantee is refused rather than pretended.
